author: CC (captured from Akien, verbatim where quoted)
relates_to: cairn/base/transitions.py (emit chokepoint, five hardcoded gate seats); cairn/build_inspector/inspector.py (FILTERS, nexus.py graft); cairn/learning_block/ (engine.py block spec, record_verdict keyed on gate); cairn/harbor_master/voyage.py (the [R]/[W]/[F]/[X]/[S] vocabulary, filed); CairnCommons/node_classes/code-seam.json (prove_gate/extra_gates as prose)
text:
THE GATE IS A TYPE, NOT A FEATURE. Akien 2026-08-05, verbatim: 'gates are dynamic. a new type of gate is extremely likely as we add new workflows. so this is a template for the whole gate-type-object we're designing... a gate has to come as "i watch for this, i inspect with that, findings must contain/not contain x, y, z, i result in new state of the other thing" and the inspectors themselves are also a learning block. their output unlocks the gate and allows the advance.' Earlier the same day, the clause it extends: 'ALL GATES ARE INSPECTORS + THE GATE. THE TICKET ARRIVING IN THE STATE TRIGGERS THE INSPECT FOR THAT GATE. THE INSPECTOR IS A SET OF FILTERS WITH AN LLM FAILOVER FOR LEARNING. IT PRODUCES FINDINGS BASED ON THE REQUIREMENTS FOR THAT GATE. THE DETERMINISTIC GATE CODE THEN WRITES THE ADVANCE TO THE TICKET.'

FOUR DECLARED PARTS, pure data, one branchless runner: (1) WATCHES — the arrival that fires it (subject, state, enter/leave, direction); (2) INSPECTS_WITH — which inspector is summoned; (3) UNLOCKS_WHEN — a predicate over the FINDINGS (must_contain / must_not_contain); (4) ADVANCES — the new state written on the named subject.

THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS, and it came from Akien: CC had proposed the gate declare `requires: [filter names]`, which is the INSPECTOR's filter set. Akien's clause 3 puts the rule on the FINDINGS instead. Those are different objects and the split is what makes gate types dynamic — a new gate reuses an existing inspector under a different acceptance rule and never touches it. Welded to a filter list, every new gate would have needed a new inspector.

AND `must_contain` CLOSES THE VACUOUS-GREEN HOLE. Today every gate in the corpus reads findings-as-refusal, so an empty finding set means pass; inspector.py:696 already carries a hand-written note about exactly this ('a gate that silently inspects nothing passes everything (Law 8)'). Under must_contain a gate may require findings to CONTAIN a green validation, not merely to lack reds — the inspector's silence stops being an unlock. Law 9 as physics rather than as a comment in one file.

'THE OTHER THING' IS LOAD-BEARING: the gate writes state on a named subject, not on itself. That is what makes it a type rather than a ticket feature — gates for workflows not yet invented get INSTANTIATED, not coded, and a gate is not welded to the workflow emitter.

INSPECTORS ARE LEARNING BLOCKS. Not a bespoke learning path per inspector: build_inspector/nexus.py (deposit_failure / counsel_failures / propose_filter) is one component re-deriving the shared organs, and re-basing it retires that (Law 1). The plumbing already anticipates this — learning_block.record_verdict(gate, ...) and pending_findings(gate=...) are ALREADY keyed on a gate, and the charter carries Akien's 2026-08-01 words for it: 'a bullet list finding from an inspector for that step that learns what --I-- will gate.' The LLM failover is at LEARNING time, never at verdict time — the verdict is always hardware (his 2026-07-28 ruling, recorded in nexus.py); a miss proposes a filter, which enters by installation.

MEASURED STATE WHEN THIS WAS DESIGNED: emit() (cairn/base/transitions.py:732) is the one chokepoint and already holds five gate seats as hardcoded `if`s — entry (into BUILDME, :770), build (out of PROVEME, :760), exit (into PROVED, :801), emission (out of WATCHME, :792), ticket-required (:772). Each already returns findings in the {filter, finding, why_it_matters, evidence} shape, complete on first pass, and the record already journals which gate ran and what it saw. So four of the five clauses are standing; what is missing is that the gate LIST is control flow rather than data, the per-gate requirements do not exist as a fact anywhere (the build gate runs all 18 FILTERS regardless of crossing), and only build_inspector can learn. The template mechanism itself is also already built and proven — engine.py's data-only block spec with a branchless runner, carrying its own falsification clause ('if expressing a block's difference ever requires code in here rather than fields in there, the hypothesis is FALSIFIED').

REWORK IN THE SIMPLIFICATION DIRECTION — Akien named this explicitly and it is the disposition, not an apology: 'even tho it's rework, it's rework in the simplification direction.' The arithmetic: five `if` branches + a bespoke nexus graft + prose gate descriptions in the node class, all replaced by one spec kind, one runner, one filter registry, one learning path. emit() ends up holding NO gate knowledge — it asks which gates watch this crossing and does what they say. This is the standing test for whether a rework is worth its cost: does the count of kinds go DOWN.

STUCK ESCALATES TO THE VIEWER, NOT TO A MANAGER. Akien 2026-08-05, closing a question CC had left open days earlier: 'what happens when things are stuck? we can see it in the harbor view. its an escalation but not to "manager" but to "viewer", in this case, for now, me. but we'll do more with this later. it will allow us to watch in real time on a web page as things move or are stuck or need more work, or whatever. eventually, we'll build mechanisms for managing all that too, with more learning blocks.' This keeps I-no-enforcer-gated-ownership intact: stuck is a thing SEEN, not a thing reported up a chain — the harbor view is a vantage, and the viewer is a seat that happens to be Akien today and becomes a learning block later. The escalation target is a ROLE, so replacing the occupant is not a redesign.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS, measured: voyage.py:25 already carries the stall vocabulary ([R] requested, [W] waiting, [F] failed, [X] refused, [S] stalled) FILED-BUT-UNEMITTED, and voyage.py:77 names '[S] starvation — the GATE-level stall, a gate with boats and no qualified subscriber' as needing an owned fact. It was filed rather than built because it had no owned fact AND no destination. Akien's answer supplies the destination. The one condition already BUILT is [~] mid-voyage (voyage.py:116) — at sea AND berthed while still in workflow, the honest silently-stuck. The surface is a declared PANE (cairn/base/device.py:114 declared_panes, cairn/base/shim.py:289), never a route or a server of harbor_master's own — one web server, per I-one-web-server-surfaces-in-the-shim.

AND THE PROBE QUESTION ANSWERS ITSELF: emit() is the one door every arrival passes through, so 'probes on all the gates' (Akien's members design, same day) is a subscription at the chokepoint, not N probes. One event, two consumers — the gate refuses-or-advances, the harbor view updates. Nothing new to instrument.

THE STUCK SUBJECT IS THE TICKET, NOT THE GATE — Akien's correction, same day, and it collapses the problem: 'its easier than that, because the gate is not stuck the ticket is. a ticket with a gate that does not exist is stuck at the start. and as we talked about before, issues a trouble ticket so we don't even have to look to know there's an issue.' CC had designed for the hard case (a boat that stopped moving — no event fires when nothing happens, so stuck would have to be DERIVED ON READ). The primary case is not that. It is STRUCTURAL and knowable at rest: the ticket declares its path, the gate table declares which crossings are watched, and a crossing in the path matching no gate is stuck before the ticket ever moves. No clock, no derivation, no waiting for silence — a validation over the declared path at cast time.

WHY IT WAS HARD GATE-SIDE AND EASY TICKET-SIDE: voyage.py:77 filed starvation as 'a gate with boats and no qualified subscriber' — gate-centric, which is why it needed an owned fact nobody owned. A gate is a type with many instances and no berth; a TICKET has an owner and an address already (Laws 5 and 6). Move the stuckness to the subject that can hold it and the owned fact stops being missing.

AND THE ESCALATION CHANNEL IS ALREADY BUILT: a trouble. 'so we don't even have to look' is literally already true — the SessionStart hook pushes every live trouble into every session open (7 standing on 2026-08-05), unasked. The trouble record's shape fits the repeat case too: count / first_seen / last_seen / occurrences, so a gate that keeps refusing the same ticket increments one trouble rather than minting many. Stuck = a trouble whose count climbs. The harbor view is then the VIEW, not the detector; the trouble store is the record of truth (Law 7).

RESIDUE, named honestly and small: the structural case is caught at cast, and the keeps-refusing case is caught at the chokepoint (a refusal IS an event). The only genuinely silent case left is a ticket nothing is ever fired at — no arrival, no refusal, no signal at all. That one still has no event, and it is the ONLY place a derive-on-read would earn its keep. Do not build for it until it is measured.

A MISSING GATE IS A DEMAND SIGNAL, NOT ONLY A DEFECT — Akien 2026-08-05, and it flips the disposition CC had just written above: 'it would make sense that the harbor master creates a gate in the view for a provider that does not yet exist online. imagine a set of books to read each as its own ticket. so we know we're gonna build a reader, and their tickets are for a reading workflow of some kind, and we unleash them... but there is no gate. and then we build the gate, and put it online, and suddenly the boats start advancing. this is a highly likely scenario or something like it when we get into bulk learning.' Unleashing work BEFORE its gate exists is a normal opening move, not an error — the tickets are the specification of what to build.

AND HIS OWN EARLIER RULE ALREADY PRODUCES IT, free: the harbor's gate roster is DEMAND-DERIVED — 'the list of gates IS the list of workflow gates each ticket is looking for, and a gate whose last ticket leaves play stops appearing' (members design, same day). A gate with boats and no implementation therefore appears by the same rule that makes an implemented gate disappear when its last boat leaves. Zero-providers and zero-boats are the two ends of one roster rule; no phantom-gate machinery is needed.

DEMAND vs MALFORMED, the structural distinguisher (needed, because a wanted-but-unbuilt gate and a typo'd crossing look identical): the PATH comes from the node class, which is authored. A crossing that appears in a declared node-class path is legitimate demand — the class asserts the workflow exists. A crossing carried by a ticket and named by NO node class is malformed. Free, no heuristic, no counting.

AGGREGATE ON THE GATE IDENTITY, NOT THE TICKET — the load-bearing detail at bulk scale. Unleash 500 books against one missing gate and the naive reading of 'issue a trouble' mints 500 troubles at session open. One trouble per MISSING GATE, count = boats waiting, occurrences = which ones. That turns the report from noise into a build queue ordered by demand, and the harbor view becomes a derived answer to what to build next rather than a planned one.

THE ONE NEW PIECE OF PHYSICS — 'suddenly the boats start advancing' does not happen by itself. The waiting boats are at rest and nothing is firing at them; the ARRIVAL that fires a gate already happened, back when there was no gate to catch it. So GATE INSTALLATION IS THE EVENT: bringing a gate online sweeps the boats whose next crossing it watches. Event-driven, not a poll — the install is the trigger.

AND THAT FORCES AN OPEN QUESTION CLOSED: from the members design, 'do providers announce through the same probe, or are they learned when one picks something up?' Bulk learning answers it — a provider MUST ANNOUNCE. If providers were only learned by picking something up, a gate arriving after its boats would never pick anything up, because everything that would have summoned it is already asleep.

THE ANATOMY OF A FUNCTIONING GATE — Akien 2026-08-05, five parts: 'a _functioning_ gate is consumers (to go thru it), plus the consumers looking for that gate (because that's what triggers appearance in the harbor), plus the inspector and his gate, and its stamp. and presumably the next one in the chain as well.'

(1) BOATS AT IT and (2) BOATS LOOKING FOR IT are DIFFERENT SETS, and the split is the load-bearing part. At-it is arrival — the cursor standing at the crossing. Looking-for-it is every boat whose DECLARED PATH names the crossing, however far downstream. Appearance in the harbor is driven by the second, which is larger and earlier: 500 books cast today all declare the reading crossing and none has reached it, so the gate must appear before any boat arrives. Built today: (1) only, as a cursor position. (2) does not exist as a fact — it needs the ticket's route as structure, which is already the queued sibling item.

(3) INSPECTOR + GATE CODE — built, but welded: five `if`s in emit() rather than instances of a type.

(4) THE STAMP — a good coinage, native to the domain (a clearance stamp in a ship's papers) and therefore derivable rather than memorized. It names something ALREADY BUILT AND ANONYMOUS: the journal record's entry_gate / build_gate / exit_gate / emission_gate notes are the stamp — the durable mark that this gate passed this boat, carrying the findings as evidence. Naming it is what lets it become a declared part of the type instead of four ad-hoc keys.

(5) THE NEXT ONE IN THE CHAIN — DERIVED, NOT DECLARED. The gate declares `advances` (a new state on a named subject); which gate comes next is whatever watches that state. A gate naming its successor would be a second copy of the routing (Law 1) and would weld gates into a fixed chain, killing the dynamic-type property that is the whole point.

BUT FUNCTIONING IS A CHAIN PROPERTY, NOT A LOCAL ONE — the sharp consequence of (5). A gate that passes boats into a state with no gate out does not unstick anything; it moves the stuck point one step downstream. So the harbor's demand list must show the whole UNBUILT RUN of the declared path, not merely the first missing gate. Build the reader gate and the fleet advances one crossing and piles up again; shown as a run, you learn the reader is N gates BEFORE starting rather than N times in a row.

ONE TROUBLE, WITH INCREMENTORS — Akien, correcting CC's framing: 'per the trouble ticket intentions, we have one ticket. it can have incrementors, but we don't get 500 tickets. we get one. one with "500 times so far starting at blahblahblah".' Already settled and already built — count / first_seen / last_seen / occurrences. The residue that is still a real choice: the aggregation key is the trouble ID, so minting the ID per BOAT would yield 500 legitimate troubles each at count=1. The ID must be the missing gate.

PREREQUISITE, and it is the same work: 'a gate that does not exist' is unaskable of five hardcoded `if`s in emit(). The question only becomes answerable once the gate list is DATA. So this check costs almost nothing once the gate-type object lands, and cannot be built before it.

SEQUENCING as it stands: the one-door skill fix first (ruled: 'prolly before... because then the next one makes use of it. we test as we go for free'), then the gate-type object, then the ticket's route+cursor as structure, then the harbor view's tap on the chokepoint. The gate-type spec's own field grammar is CC's to settle against the question corpus; the instances come back to Akien when they are expressible.
